result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend container queries in their first sentence and use the three placements to show why the viewport can't tell the card how much room it has. B wins because it names real limits of the approach: inline-size containment can break a modal that shrinks to fit its content, the extra setup, designers having to think in card widths, and where media queries still apply. A mostly says browser support isn't a concern. A has the more concrete CSS snippet and is slightly tighter, but it is weaker on trade-offs. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend container queries right away and use the three placements to show why viewport queries fail. A names more real trade-offs: inline-size containment can break a modal that shrinks to fit its content, teams have to plan around card widths, and media queries are still right for some things. A also notes that the 4-up row can collapse to 1-up, so the card can be wide on a small screen. B has a more concrete snippet and useful testing tips, but it is slightly longer and covers fewer limits of the approach.
